segment.description: New River, Scott County, in the New River-Clear Fork system of the South Fork Cumberland basin (HUC 05130104); catalog notes it runs its full named length (Scott/Anderson counties) down to the Clear Fork confluence country. Acid-buffered plateau freestone, rain-driven flows. This is the Scott County New River, not the West Virginia New River.
segment.boundaries: Catalog covers the named river; the on-reach USGS gauge 03408500 'NEW RIVER AT NEW RIVER, TN' sits at 36.38553, -84.55470 (382 sq mi drainage).

coldSource.notes: USGS 03408500 'NEW RIVER AT NEW RIVER, TN': Scott County (FIPS 151), HUC 05130104, altitude 1,092.01 ft NAVD88, drainage 382 sq mi, free-flowing river station (verified via waterservices expanded site output: https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?sites=03408500&siteOutput=expanded&format=rdb). The river is NOT on TDEC's Tennessee Scenic Rivers index (index consulted 2026-09-18; no New River entry among its 24 named waters): https://www.tn.gov/environment/natural-areas/tn-scenic-rivers.html

holdover.detail: No holdover is possible to document: the water has no TWRA trout stocking program at all (no New River row in the 2026 row-level TWRA stocking schedule; the only '(NEW)' tags on the schedule page are newness labels for other waters).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild-trout status: the river is absent from TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list (that list covers Monroe/Carter/Johnson/Greene/Unicoi county waters only) and no trout survey record for this New River was found.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The on-reach USGS gauge recorded 29.9 C water in July 2025 and TWRA maintains no trout stocking, wild-trout status, or special regulation for this New River.
